Checking the share skill, new-repo skill, and MCP tools for create_project and move_agent_to_root.

GetMcpTools was unavailable in this subagent context. I am now reviewing the cloud-agent documentation and help files on conversation search across workspaces. Side chats remain attached to their parent workspace. File > Open Folder is the official way to open a project.

No official button exists to continue a chat in another folder. Agents Window is the documented multi-workspace surface, and conversation search runs there via Ctrl+K. Chat history is strictly workspace-scoped; opening a different folder creates a new workspace ID, so chats do not transfer. Adding folders to the workspace can also alter the workspace ID.

Forking copies a conversation into a new chat inside the same workspace. It does not transfer across workspaces.

The @Chats reference feature stays within the current workspace.

Shared transcripts via the Share icon generate a forked version. This is a Teams or Enterprise feature. It does not move the original chat. Local files are excluded.

Moving an agent to the cloud transfers conversation history. It does not preserve unsaved local changes.

`create_project` and `move_agent_to_root` are MCP tools on `cursor-app-control`, not documented user workflows. They migrate the composer and chat to a new folder. They are buggy in 2026, especially with multi-root workspaces. The official workaround is to open a single-folder window or avoid calling the tool.

File > Add Folder to Workspace is not recommended for keeping one chat across repositories. It is tied to the first folder in a multi-root workspace, so adding folders can sever history linkage. Multi-root workspaces also trigger the buggy `move_agent_to_root` tool and may cause the agent to abort. The official cross-repo experience is Agents Window, and Cloud Agents provide explicit multi-repo environments. Agent transcripts are stored in `~/.cursor/projects/` on Windows.

Keep this chat in `bowlyzer_deploy`. Do not **File > Open Folder** on `bowlyzer-api` if you want the same thread. That opens a new workspace, so the IDE chat list does not follow.

### Practical steps (Cursor Desktop, Windows)

**To keep this conversation going**

1. Stay in the current window (repo A).
2. Create `bowlyzer-api` as a sibling folder.
3. Point the agent at B with `@` folders or absolute paths (`C:\Users\cfell\repositories\bowlyzer-api\...`).
4. Optional: **File > Add Folder to Workspace** → pick B, then **File > Save Workspace As…** and always reopen that `.code-workspace`. That keeps the same workspace identity (and this chat) only if A stays the first folder.

**If you open B as its own window**

- This chat will not appear there.
- In **Agents Window** (`Ctrl+Shift+P` → Open Agents Window), press **Ctrl+K** to search past transcripts, or `@Chats` in a new thread.
- Fork/duplicate only copies the thread **inside the same workspace**. Shared-transcript **Fork to Cursor** (Teams/Enterprise) copies history, not local files.

**What transfers vs what does not**

| Transfers | Does not transfer |
|---|---|
| Message history in this window / Agents Window search | Semantic index, `@` files, `.cursor/rules`, `AGENTS.md` of the other repo |
| CLI `agent ls` / resume of the same thread | Checkpoints (file snapshots for this checkout) |
| Cloud “Move to Cloud”: conversation text | Dirty/uncommitted files |

**File > Add Folder to Workspace is not the documented recommended way.** Official Desktop guidance is **File > Open Folder** for a project, and **Agents Window** for working across repos. Multi-root can keep one chat if you never change how you open it, but it is fragile (history is keyed off workspace path / first folder).

**`create_project` / `move_agent_to_root`:** agent/MCP tools (chat menu **Move to**, UI “Switching workspace root”). Not a documented user workflow, and in 2026 they often abort or freeze mid-turn—especially in multi-root. Do not rely on them. Cursor’s own workaround is: stay put with absolute paths, or open B with **File > Open Folder** and start a **new** chat.

---

**Short reply you can send**

Stay in this `bowlyzer_deploy` window so this chat keeps going. Create `bowlyzer-api` next to it and `@`-mention that folder (or add it with File > Add Folder to Workspace and save a `.code-workspace`). Opening B alone starts a new workspace: the transcript does not follow, and B’s index/rules/checkpoints are separate. Agents Window (`Ctrl+K`) can find old chats; don’t use agent “Move to” / `move_agent_to_root`.
